_preservation.source: Captured from Isj's Neon console output, relayed through the orchestrator. NOT a live SELECT run by this agent. The production Booking table was emptied after this capture (verified in the same console: bookings 0, muhurat 0, payouts 0, reviews 0), so this file is the only surviving copy of these nine rows.
_preservation.completeness: All nine rows, complete. An earlier draft of this file recorded rows 7-8 as LOST — they were not lost, only unrelayed. Corrected.
_preservation.why_this_matters: Three pricing eras are visible here, and each is a decision otherwise reconstructable only from commit messages. THE 15% ERA (rows 1-8): commission 15%, charged to the customer ON TOP *and* deducted from the pandit — the double-charge — with 18% GST on the fee shown as a separate customer line. THE RATE CUT (commit 0be83f5, 15 July, 'commission is ONE number (10%)') is why row 9 alone derives 10%. THE MODEL-A ERA closes with row 9 (20 July): fee NOT on top, pandit absorbs it. Ruling B (commit 3548679, 22 July) reversed that two days later, so row 9 is the last and only production artefact of the deducted model. travelCost is 0 on all nine — no real customer money ever moved through the fabricated travel path.

_two_source_check.method: derived_fee_pct = Math.round(platformFee * 100 / dakshinaAmount), cross-checked against the 2026-07-15 rate boundary (commit 0be83f5). Computed in Node, not Python — Python's round() uses banker's rounding and produced a FALSE mismatch on row 8 (round(40.5)=40) where JavaScript's Math.round(40.5)=41 matches the stored value. The runtime that produced the data is the runtime that must check it.
_two_source_check.result: PASS on all nine. Rows 1-8 derive 15%, row 9 derives 10%. Both sources agree everywhere; no row required a fallback.
_two_source_check.gst_rounding_tell: Math.round(fee * 0.18) reproduces the stored GST on rows 2,3,4,6,7,8. It does NOT on rows 1 and 5, where 465*0.18=83.7 rounds to 84 but 83 is stored. Those two are the only seed rows whose GST is fractional, and a human truncated. That single rupee is what distinguishes hand-written fixtures from computed output.

_producing_path_trace.rows_1_to_6: HAND-WRITTEN LITERALS in packages/db/prisma/seed.ts (created within ~2s of each other, 2026-07-08T19:03:28-30). seed.ts:284 writes `dakshinaAmount: 3100, platformFee: 465, platformFeeGst: 83, grandTotal: 3648` directly. Confirmed by the 83-vs-84 tell above.
_producing_path_trace.rows_7_and_8: PRODUCED BY THE REAL SERVER CODE PATH. services/api/scripts/stage-pilot-fixtures.mjs (committed 805d78e, 2026-07-14) imports bookingService.createBooking and paymentService.processPaymentSuccess — its own comment says these are 'the exact function POST /bookings calls' and 'the exact function the Razorpay verify/webhook' calls — and invokes them with pay_pilot_manual / order_pilot_manual and pay_notifyproof / order_notifyproof. Every figure reproduces exactly under the 14-July constants (PLATFORM_FEE_PERCENT = 15, GST_PERCENT = 18) and the pre-f803f10 expressions.
_producing_path_trace.CONCLUSION: THE DOUBLE-CHARGE WAS REAL PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR, NOT MERELY POSSIBLE. Rows 7 and 8 were computed by the live pricing code on 14 July: grandTotal = dakshina + fee + gst (fee ON TOP) AND panditPayout = dakshina - fee (fee ALSO deducted). Two bookings were priced that way through the real service functions. Commit f803f10 (16 July) killed the model two days later, naming it: 'The old model double-charged: +10% on the customer AND -10% from the pandit.' No real customer was involved — both are pilot-rehearsal fixtures — but the code that priced them was the shipped code.
_producing_path_trace.rows_9: The live customer wizard (specialInstructions 'P-PAY E2E test-mode proof run', razorpayOrderId order_TFefNl2TrhDM3E). Matches the 20-July code exactly: gst 0 (GST-inclusive since f803f10) and grandTotal == dakshina (Model A, fee not on top).
_producing_path_trace.correction_recorded: An earlier pass in this campaign ran the arithmetic on row 1, saw it agree with the pre-16-July model, and was about to name that code as the producer. Checking seed.ts reversed it for rows 1-6. The SAME arithmetic, applied to rows 7-8 where no seed literal exists and a script calling the real services does, now confirms the code path. Arithmetic agreement is evidence, never a producing path — the path has to be named.

_operational_notes.row_5_refund: HPJ-005 carries refundStatus COMPLETED with refundAmount 0 — a completed refund of nothing. A seed artefact; no refund path produced it.
_operational_notes.row_7_acceptedAt: HPJ-2026-80714 has acceptedAt 2026-07-14T07:32:31.506, eight minutes after creation. THE ACCEPT PATH GENUINELY EXECUTED ONCE IN PRODUCTION. This is the only production evidence that the pandit accept loop ever ran end to end, and it feeds the open accept-route trace (the singular /pandit/bookings/:id/accept vs the plural registration at app.ts:409).
_operational_notes.payout_zero: panditPayout is 0 on rows 2,4,5,6 despite CAPTURED payments — those rows never reached a payout computation. Rows 1,3,7,8,9 carry real payout figures.
_operational_notes.duplicate_legacy_columns: Every row carries empty-string customerName / customerPhone / eventAddress / pujaType — duplicate legacy columns alongside the real relations.
